summary.name: Manga (category: Drawing and Illustration; provenance explicit). The source directly describes this manga visual direction, though some source prompts are partial.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit: monochrome or limited-color manga style with controlled line-weight hierarchy, screentone shading, expressive panels, and close-ups. Screentone scale must stay consistent, and lettering must stay readable. A generic dot filter must not be applied to every surface.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: manga-inspired video and interactive HTML using panel reveals, poses, and targeted speed effects. Inferred from listed examples: story trailers, dramatic reveal moments, webtoon-style promos, educational manga, and onboarding guides. Inferred suitability is not a source requirement.
summary.limitations: Strongest in strict black-and-white with stable screentone. Hybrids are advised only for close-up depth or instructional annotation. Do not scale tones into moiré, add gray gradients for depth, or apply parallax to every panel. Duration, aspect ratio, and resolution are unspecified; source values are optional examples.
summary.palette: Suggested, not supplied: background #FFFFFF and foreground #171717, two base colors, no gradient. Apparent gray comes from screentones, not extra hues. Two-color contrast is 17.928:1, meeting the 4.5 normal-text target. Task-supplied colors override these, and composited frames must be rechecked. Chroma-js 3.2.0 is used for validation.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit: animate panel reveals, poses, and targeted speed effects. The motion engine owns trajectories and easing, with one owner per animated property. Video drives motion from composition time; interactive delivery may add pointer or scroll input. Motion-016 (cinematic opening with separable subject, speed-line, and text layers) is preferred when those layers exist. Motion-006 needs eye layers or a rig. Motion-012 and motion-015 suit chapter transitions and storytelling.
summary.audio: Unspecified by the source for this style. Audio should be proposed from the topic, audience, and motion, and gallery demos may stay silent. Inferred options include restrained impact accents, page or ink sounds, or voiceover. Speech must remain intelligible, avoid clipping, and stay synchronized with picture. Honor any user-supplied audio requirements first.
summary.assetRequirements: Separate line art, screentones, panels, and lettering into distinct layers. Keep screentone spacing stable during masking, scaling, and pose changes. Preserve supplied artwork, exact colors, and authored transforms. Load fonts and assets before rendering. Cache stateful simulations. Missing assets must be stated. Asset formats and sizes are unspecified.
summary.combinations: Manga is strongest alone. Optional hybrid style-101 adds parallax planes to selected hero close-ups with unchanged screentone scale and small offsets. Optional style-024 adds handwritten margin notes in #171717 only, with line weight below panel contours and no overlap with speech balloons. Avoid colored highlighters and added gradients.
summary.productionApproach: Style renderer (SVG recommended; Python with Pillow for masks and textures) owns drawing and materials. Motion engine (GSAP for seekable timelines; Motion optional) owns animation. HyperFrames is the default pipeline for assembly, timing, audio sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when its documented condition is met, with the reason recorded. Verify key frames, direct seeks, and full decoded playback.
